sentences.text: Archaeotriakis was an extinct false catshark known primarily from isolated teeth.
This animal belongs to the class Chondrichthyes and is part of the family Triakidae.
The genus was described by Case in 1978.

It includes two species: Archaeotriakis rochelleae, described from the Judith River Formation of Montana, and Archaeotriakis ornatus, originally described from the Teapot Member of the Mesaverde Group in Wyoming.
It lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago, within the Western Interior Seaway in North America.
Fossils of Archaeotriakis ornatus have also been found in the Bearpaw Formation of Alberta, Canada.
